name: Honduras Organic 18 Rabbit Yellow Honey
vendor_notes: Mild floral notes, very sweet, creamy body with honeysuckle. Brightness 6/7, sweetness 6/7, body 1/7. CoE top-10 finalist farm.
goal: Sweet, bright, floral light roast for espresso with some body
rationale: Lower altitude (1,400 m) Catuai is less dense than the Ethiopian, and honey processing leaves fruit sugars on the bean. It browns faster and can scorch or tip if the start is too hot, so it charges cooler (188 C) with a slightly gentler burner. Body is listed as very light (1/7), which makes thin espresso, so this plan gives it a little more Maillard time and development (DTR ~19%, ~11 C after FC) to build sweetness and body without losing the honeysuckle. Honey coffees have more chaff and smoke, so air comes up a bit earlier.
steps: Preheat SV 188 C for 20 min. Drum 90, air 30.
Charge 170 g at BT ~188 C. Burner 85%, air 30.
TP ~1:00 near 98 C. RoR should peak ~23 C/min around 2:00.
At ~170 C (~5:40): burner 65%, air 50 (clears honey-process chaff/smoke).
~30 s before FC (~179 C): burner 55%. No hard cut at FC.
FC ~7:00 at ~185 C: burner 50%, air 55. RoR drifts ~9 -> 4.
Drop ~8:40 at ~196 C (about 11 C after FC).

history.note: Initial plan from vendor data (Coffee Bean Corral) and Kaleido M1 behaviour. FC temperature is a guess until your first roast calibrates the probe.
